Additional Notes:
- UV Index will be extreme (11), so use protection if you go outside.
- Air quality will be good.
- No rain is expected.

content.text:
Here's a weather outlook for your trip from Dallas to Houston next week:

Dallas:
- Generally hot and sunny with highs around 37–38°C (98–100°F).
- Mostly clear skies, almost no rain expected.
- UV Index is extreme—sun protection is important!
- Air quality is good, but pollen and mold counts may be moderate to high.
- Nights are warm, around 26°C (79°F).

Houston:
- Also hot, though slightly cooler than Dallas with highs 33–36°C (91–97°F).
- Greater humidity and a higher chance for afternoon thunderstorms.
    - Rain/T-storm chances are highest August 7–9 and August 11, with a 40–55% probability for stray storms in the afternoon.
- UV Index is extreme.
- Air quality is mostly good.
- Nights are humid and warm (around 25°C/77°F).

Tips:
- Plan for hot, humid weather and strong sun along the whole route.
- Watch for scattered afternoon thunderstorms (especially in Houston), which can cause sudden downpours and slow traffic.
- Stay hydrated and protect yourself from the sun!
- If driving, keep an eye on weather alerts for pop-up storms, especially as you approach Houston.

Let me know the exact dates if you want a day-by-day breakdown! Safe travels!

- Los Angeles is UTC-8 during Standard Time and UTC-7 during Daylight Saving Time.
- Beijing is always UTC+8 (no Daylight Saving Time).

- 16 hours when Los Angeles is on Standard Time (PST)
- 15 hours when Los Angeles is on Daylight Saving Time (PDT)

- 15 hours when Los Angeles is on Daylight Saving Time (PDT)
